default_instructions: After food

name: Aceclofenac 100mg + Paracetamol 325mg
default_instructions: After food

name: Tramadol 50mg
default_instructions: After food

name: Rabeprazole 20mg + Domperidone 30mg

name: Trypsin + Chymotrypsin
default_instructions: Before food
description: Enzyme combination to reduce inflammation and oedema.

name: Chlorhexidine 1% Dental Gel
default_instructions: Apply locally to affected gums.
description: Topical antiseptic gel for gingival and periodontal conditions.

name: Lignocaine 2% Gel
default_instructions: Apply locally to painful area as needed.
description: Topical anaesthetic gel for oral ulcers and localized pain.

name: Vitamin B-Complex
default_instructions: After food
description: Nutritional supplement to support oral mucosal healing.

name: Vitamin C 500mg
default_instructions: After food
description: Supports gum health and wound healing.

name: Amoxicillin Syrup 125mg/5ml
default_instructions: After food. Shake well before use. (Paediatric)
description: Paediatric antibiotic suspension for dental infections in children.

name: Paracetamol Syrup 125mg/5ml
default_instructions: After food. (Paediatric)
description: Paediatric analgesic and antipyretic suspension.

name: Ibuprofen Syrup 100mg/5ml
default_instructions: After food. (Paediatric)
description: Paediatric NSAID suspension for pain and fever.

name: Clindamycin 300mg
default_instructions: After food with plenty of water
description: Antibiotic for dental infections in penicillin-allergic patients.

name: Ornidazole 500mg
default_instructions: After food
description: Antiprotozoal and anti-anaerobic agent for periodontal infections.

name: Triamcinolone Acetonide 0.1% Oral Paste
default_instructions: Apply a thin film to ulcer at bedtime.
description: Topical corticosteroid paste for aphthous ulcers and oral lesions.

name: Lignocaine 2% Injection (Xylocaine)
default_instructions: For infiltration/nerve block use only. Fast onset, moderate duration.
description: Most versatile amide local anaesthetic; infiltration, nerve blocks, extradural and spinal blocks.

name: Bupivacaine 0.5% Injection (Sensorcaine)
default_instructions: For infiltration/nerve block use only. Longer duration; separates sensory from motor block.
description: Amide local anaesthetic with long duration of action; used for prolonged post-operative pain relief.

name: Prilocaine 4% Injection (Citanest)
default_instructions: For infiltration/nerve block use only. Least systemic toxicity of the amides.
description: Amide local anaesthetic with fast onset and least systemic toxicity; caution with methaemoglobinaemia at high doses.

name: Mepivacaine 3% Injection (Carbocaine)
default_instructions: For infiltration/nerve block use only. Suitable when vasoconstrictor is to be avoided.
description: Amide local anaesthetic; versatile with moderate vasodilation, useful for infiltration and peripheral nerve blocks.

name: Aspirin 350mg (Ecosprin)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid in bleeding disorders or peptic ulcer.
description: Salicylate NSAID; analgesic, antipyretic and anti-inflammatory action for mild to moderate dental pain.

name: Mefenamic Acid 500mg (Meftal)
default_instructions: After food. Not for use beyond one week.
description: Anthranilic acid NSAID with peripheral and central analgesic action; effective for post-extraction and traumatic dental pain.

name: Naproxen 250mg (Naprosyn)
default_instructions: After food
description: Propionic acid NSAID for dental pain and inflammation.

name: Ketoprofen 100mg (Ostofen)
default_instructions: After food
description: Propionic acid NSAID for moderate dental pain and inflammation.

name: Piroxicam 20mg (Dolonex)
default_instructions: After food
description: Oxicam NSAID; reversible COX inhibitor for short-term analgesia and long-term anti-inflammatory use.

name: Nimesulide 100mg (Nimulid)
default_instructions: After food. Not recommended below 12 years.
description: Preferential COX-2 inhibitor NSAID with rapid onset; used for acute dental pain and post-surgical inflammation.

name: Celecoxib 200mg (Celact)
default_instructions: After food. Contains a sulfonamide moiety; avoid in sulfa allergy.
description: Selective COX-2 inhibitor with reduced GI and platelet effects; used for patients needing longer-term pain relief.

name: Ampicillin 500mg (Ampilin)
default_instructions: Before food, empty stomach
description: Aminopenicillin antibiotic for dental and mixed infections.

name: Amoxicillin + Clavulanic Acid 1g (Augmentin)
default_instructions: Deep I.M. or I.V. 6-8 hourly, as per severity.
description: Injectable beta-lactamase inhibitor combination for severe dental/oro-facial infections.

name: Cefixime 200mg (Topcef)
default_instructions: After food
description: Third-generation oral cephalosporin for dental infections resistant to first-line antibiotics.

name: Cefpodoxime Proxetil 200mg (Cepodem)
default_instructions: After food
description: Third-generation oral cephalosporin for moderate to severe dental infections.

name: Cefuroxime Axetil 500mg (Ceftum)
default_instructions: After food
description: Second-generation oral cephalosporin for dental and soft tissue infections.

name: Cefadroxil 500mg (Droxyl)
default_instructions: After food
description: First-generation cephalosporin antibiotic, alternative to cephalexin.

name: Tetracycline 250mg (Achromycin)
default_instructions: Before food, empty stomach with plenty of water. Avoid in pregnancy and children under 8 years (tooth discolouration).
description: Tetracycline-class antibiotic; broad spectrum, avoided in pregnancy/young children due to dental staining.

name: Oxytetracycline 250mg (Terramycin)
default_instructions: Before food, empty stomach. Avoid in pregnancy and children under 8 years (tooth discolouration).
description: Tetracycline-class antibiotic for mixed infections; avoided in pregnancy and young children.

name: Chloramphenicol 500mg
default_instructions: After food. Reserve for serious infections; monitor for bone marrow suppression.
description: Broad-spectrum antibiotic reserved for serious infections (e.g. enteric fever, anaerobic infections); risk of aplastic anaemia.

name: Sulfadiazine 500mg
default_instructions: After food with plenty of water.
description: Short-acting sulfonamide antibiotic; rarely used alone, mainly in combination therapy.

name: Cotrimoxazole 960mg (Trimethoprim + Sulfamethoxazole)
default_instructions: After food with plenty of water.
description: Synergistic combination antibiotic for urinary, respiratory and mixed bacterial infections.

name: Ciprofloxacin 500mg (Cifran)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid antacids/dairy within 2 hours.
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic for serious bacterial infections; occasional use in oro-facial infections.

name: Norfloxacin 400mg (Norflox)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid antacids/dairy within 2 hours.
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic, primarily for urinary and genital tract infections.

name: Ofloxacin 200mg
default_instructions: After food. Avoid antacids/dairy within 2 hours.
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic for respiratory, ENT and genitourinary infections.

name: Levofloxacin 500mg (Lomecon)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid antacids/dairy within 2 hours.
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic for respiratory and soft tissue infections.

name: Gatifloxacin 400mg (Zanocin)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid antacids/dairy within 2 hours.
description: Fluoroquinolone antibiotic for community acquired pneumonia and chronic bronchitis.

name: Streptomycin 1g Injection
default_instructions: Deep I.M. injection. Monitor for ototoxicity with prolonged use.
description: Aminoglycoside antibiotic for tuberculosis, endocarditis, plague; risk of ototoxicity.

name: Gentamicin 80mg Injection (Garamycin)
default_instructions: I.M. injection, 8 hourly or as directed. Monitor renal function.
description: Aminoglycoside antibiotic for severe gram-negative infections; nephrotoxic and ototoxic risk.

name: Tobramycin 80mg Injection (Tobacin)
default_instructions: I.M. injection, as directed. Monitor renal and auditory function.
description: Aminoglycoside antibiotic for serious Pseudomonas and Proteus infections.

name: Erythromycin 500mg (Erythrocin)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid with terfenadine.
description: Macrolide antibiotic; alternative to penicillin in hypersensitive patients.

name: Clarithromycin 500mg (Claribid)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid in pregnancy.
description: Macrolide antibiotic for respiratory, sinus and soft tissue infections; alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

name: Nystatin Oral Suspension (Mycostatin)

name: Clotrimazole 1% Oral Gel (Candid)
default_instructions: Apply locally to affected oral mucosa after food.
description: Imidazole antifungal for topical oral candidiasis.

name: Ketoconazole 200mg (Nizral)
default_instructions: After food. Monitor liver function with prolonged use.
description: Imidazole antifungal for oral/pharyngeal candidiasis, especially in immunocompromised patients.

name: Miconazole 2% Oral Gel (Daktarin)
default_instructions: Apply locally to affected areas after food; retain in mouth before swallowing.
description: Imidazole antifungal gel for oral and cutaneous candidiasis.

name: Amphotericin B Oral Suspension (Fungizone)
default_instructions: Swish in mouth and swallow, after food. For oral thrush only (oral route is non-toxic).
description: Polyene antifungal; oral suspension used for oral candidiasis, virtually non-toxic by this route.

name: Griseofulvin 500mg (Grisovin-FP)
default_instructions: After fatty food to improve absorption.
description: Systemic antifungal for dermatophytosis; not typically used for oral candidiasis.

name: Acyclovir 200mg (Zovirax)
default_instructions: After food with plenty of water. Start as early as possible after lesion onset.
description: First-line antiviral for herpes simplex infections of the lips and gums (herpetic gingivostomatitis).

name: Acyclovir 5% Skin Cream (Cyclovir)
default_instructions: Apply locally to cold sores/lesions. May cause transient stinging.
description: Topical antiviral cream for herpes labialis (cold sores).

name: Famciclovir 500mg (Famtrex)
default_instructions: After food.
description: Antiviral for herpes simplex and herpes zoster infections; alternative to acyclovir.

name: Ganciclovir Injection
default_instructions: I.V. infusion under supervision, for severe cytomegalovirus/herpes infections.
description: Antiviral reserved for severe cytomegalovirus and resistant herpes infections.

name: Foscarnet Injection

description: Antiviral used for acyclovir-resistant herpes simplex/zoster infections.

name: Zidovudine 300mg (Retrovir)
default_instructions: After food. Used in combination antiretroviral therapy under physician supervision.
description: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in combination antiretroviral therapy for HIV.

name: Didanosine 100mg (Dinex)
default_instructions: Before food, on empty stomach. Part of combination antiretroviral therapy.
description: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor for HIV, used in combination therapy.

name: Stavudine 30mg (Stavir)
default_instructions: After food. Part of combination antiretroviral therapy.
description: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor for HIV, used in combination therapy.

name: Lamivudine 150mg (Lamivir)
default_instructions: After food. Part of combination antiretroviral/antihepatitis therapy.
description: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used for HIV and chronic hepatitis B.

name: Absorbable Gelatin Sponge
default_instructions: Cut and apply directly to bleeding surface/extraction site. Do not over-pack.
description: Local absorbable haemostat; forms mechanical matrix for clotting at capillary-level bleeding, e.g. post-extraction sockets.

name: Collagen Haemostat
default_instructions: Apply directly to bleeding surface with pressure; may be moistened with saline. Do not use in infected sites.
description: Local absorbable haemostat pad; applied directly with pressure to control post-extraction/surgical bleeding.

name: Oxidized Cellulose
default_instructions: Apply dry to bleeding surface for immediate haemorrhage control. Not for fracture sites.
description: Local absorbable haemostat; most effective applied dry, used for immediate control of surface haemorrhage.

name: Desmopressin Acetate
default_instructions: Give 30 minutes preoperatively as directed for Haemophilia A/Von Willebrand disease. Monitor fluid intake.
description: Systemic haemostatic used preoperatively in Haemophilia A and Von Willebrand disease to reduce bleeding risk.

name: Tranexamic Acid 500mg
default_instructions: After food. Continue post-surgery until bleeding controlled. Avoid in subarachnoid haemorrhage.
description: Antifibrinolytic; prevents clot breakdown, used peri/post-operatively for patients at high bleeding risk (e.g. anticoagulated patients).

name: Aminocaproic Acid 500mg
default_duration: Until bleeding controlled (up to 8 hrs initial course)
default_instructions: After food. Avoid rapid I.V. infusion. Monitor for haematuria of upper urinary origin.
description: Antifibrinolytic used to control excessive bleeding, alternative to tranexamic acid.

name: Thrombin Topical (Powder/Solution)
default_instructions: Apply topically to bleeding skin/mucosal surface only. Never inject into blood vessels.
description: Topical haemostatic agent for profuse surface bleeding; forms fibrin directly at the bleeding site.

name: Aluminium Chloride 20% Gel/Solution

description: Gingival retraction cord impregnated with aluminium chloride astringent.

name: Aluminium Potassium Sulphate Powder
default_instructions: Apply directly to gingival tissue via cotton pledget or retraction cord.
description: Astringent for gingival retraction; limited use due to milder astringent properties.

name: Aluminium Sulphate Cotton Pellet
default_instructions: Apply directly to gingival tissue with cotton pledget or impregnated retraction cord.
description: Astringent and haemostatic agent for gingival retraction, available as cotton pellet, gel or impregnated cord.

name: Ferric Chloride Solution
default_instructions: Apply directly to tissue with cotton pledget or gingival retraction cord.
description: Astringent solution for gingival retraction.

name: Ferric Subsulphate Solution
default_instructions: Apply directly to tissue with cotton pledget or gingival retraction cord.
description: Astringent solution for gingival retraction, similar to ferric sulphate.

name: Ferric Sulphate Solution
default_instructions: Apply directly to tissue with cotton pledget or gingival retraction cord. May cause more tissue injury than aluminium compounds.
description: Effective astringent and haemostatic for gingival retraction; more irritating to tissue than aluminium-based astringents.

name: Ferric Sulphate/Subsulphate Solution 25%
default_instructions: Apply directly to tissue with cotton pledget or gingival retraction cord.
description: 25% astringent solution for gingival retraction and haemostasis.

name: Retraction Cord, Plain
default_instructions: Use as directed for mechanical gingival retraction prior to impressions.
description: Plain gingival retraction cord without astringent medicament.

name: Retraction Paste, Plain
default_instructions: Use as directed for gingival retraction prior to impressions.
description: Plain gingival retraction paste without astringent medicament.

name: Retraction Paste with Aluminium Chloride 6.5%
default_instructions: Use as directed. Check for history of allergy; may cause irritation or tissue destruction.
description: Astringent gingival retraction paste for use prior to impressions or restorations.

name: Retraction Cord with Aluminium Sulphate
default_instructions: Use as directed for gingival retraction. May cause irritation or caustic effect.
description: Gingival retraction cord impregnated with aluminium sulphate astringent.

name: Retraction Cord with Aluminium Potassium Sulphate
default_instructions: Use as directed for gingival retraction. May cause irritation.
description: Gingival retraction cord impregnated with aluminium potassium sulphate astringent.

name: Retraction Cord with Epinephrine (0.5mg/in)
default_instructions: Use as directed. Avoid in patients with cardiovascular disease, hypertension, hyperthyroidism, diabetes or arteriosclerosis.
description: Gingival retraction cord with epinephrine for vasoconstriction; contraindicated in cardiovascular/endocrine disease due to systemic absorption risk.

name: Atropine Sulphate
default_instructions: Give 60-90 minutes before impression/restoration to time peak antisialagogue effect. Avoid in glaucoma, prostatic hypertrophy.
description: Anticholinergic; reduces salivation before restorative procedures requiring a dry field.

name: Glycopyrrolate 1mg
default_instructions: Give 45-75 minutes before impression/restoration to reduce salivation. Avoid in acute glaucoma, severe ulcerative colitis.
description: Anticholinergic antisialagogue for controlling salivation during dry-field restorative procedures.

name: Pilocarpine Hydrochloride 5mg
default_instructions: After food. For xerostomia/Sjogren's syndrome. Avoid in uncontrolled asthma.
description: Cholinergic sialogogue used to stimulate saliva production in xerostomia and Sjogren's syndrome.

name: Triclosan 0.03% Mouthwash
default_instructions: Rinse 10ml for 1 minute after brushing, then spit out. Do not swallow. Avoid food/drink for 30 minutes.
description: First-generation antiplaque mouthwash; delays plaque maturation and inhibits inflammatory prostaglandin/leukotriene formation.

name: Delmopinol 0.2% Mouthwash
default_instructions: Rinse 10ml for 1 minute, then spit out. Do not swallow. Avoid food/drink for 30 minutes.
description: Third-generation antiplaque mouthwash with superior retentive properties over second-generation agents; reduces plaque and bacterial adhesion.

name: Sodium Fluoride 0.05% Anticavity Rinse
default_instructions: Rinse 10ml for 1 minute daily after brushing, then spit out. Do not swallow. Not for children under 6 years.
description: Therapeutic anticavity fluoride rinse for caries prevention, used daily as an adjunct to brushing.
